before_taxonomy.classification_basis: Investigators submitted a low-resolution surveillance image to facial recognition, obtained 73 candidates and selected Woodruff as an investigative lead through human narrowing and peer review. A witness then selected her from a separately prepared photo lineup; a captain, prosecutor and magistrate approved the subsequent warrant. The actual arrest was of the wrong person, but these intervening decisions prevent treating the model result as automatic arrest authority. The August 2025 court expressly did not decide whether the facial-recognition lead tainted the witness's later selection; the independent evidentiary validity of that authority basis is therefore unresolved. This materially engages Inferential Evidence–Authority Separation without demonstrating either impermissible promotion of model inference into binding authority or adequate independence of the later coercive decision. The facial-recognition investigative lead received documented peer review, and a separately prepared photo lineup was administered before the warrant. Those verification steps occurred; the later incorrect arrest does not itself establish that a required check was omitted. The court record does not supply a complete contemporaneous methodology for narrowing 73 candidates, nor establish that a particular additional identity or lineup-independence check was mandatory and omitted before a completed verification claim. The court also declined to decide the ACLU's proposed facial-recognition-taint argument. Required Verification Completion is materially engaged at the point where an AI-sourced lead acquired investigative assurance, but the specific required-unperformed-check condition and a positively adequate success-side verification chain remain unestablished. The facial-recognition search returned 73 candidates from a low-definition camera image, investigators narrowed that output to one suspect through peer review, and the witness then selected the same person in a separate lineup. The resulting information reached a high-consequence warrant workflow. The court record does not reconstruct the ranking methodology or establish whether the witness lineup was independent of the machine-generated lead; it also notes the later arrest was of the wrong person. These gaps materially engage the sufficiency of epistemic assurance for consequential reliance, but the warrant was not based on a facial match alone: intervening corroborative processes and judicial approvals were documented. The court found probable cause was not disproven on the submitted claims and left the lineup-taint question undecided. The exact unacceptable-assurance threshold or an affirmatively adequate independent reliance decision is not proven, so no failure or successful-invariant polarity is asserted.

evidence_search.notes: Current screen reads the repository-preserved source-attributed evidence and complete episode inventory. It does not claim fresh full-text access to every originating source. No canonical restamp or independent source verification is implied.

episode_inventory.purpose: Separate investigative nomination, witness checking, warrant authorisation, arrest, attempted correction, release and later disposition. Preserve the distinction between a mistaken lead and demonstrated evidence-to-authority conversion.

clauses.source_paraphrase: After a 29 January carjacking report, police reviewed video of a woman returning the victim’s phone. On 1 February, Oliver submitted extracted images for facial-recognition searching.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: The investigative image and the offence account establish the task context. They do not independently identify the person to be arrested.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The facial-recognition search produced 73 candidates and an investigator narrowed them to Woodruff as the investigative lead; the selection was peer reviewed.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Human narrowing and peer review of machine-generated candidates remain part of the originating inferential process and do not, by themselves, establish an independent identity basis for coercive action. Reliance on the nominated identity also requires assurance calibrated to the arrest workflow.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The February 2 search produced 73 candidate identities, followed by human narrowing and peer review. That machine nomination entered a consequential investigative chain, but no warrant was issued at this stage; the intervening witness lineup and official approvals mean that sufficient inferential promotion into coercive authority is not established here alone.

A lower-quality surveillance image produced 73 biometric candidates, then a narrowed suspect lead. Peer review occurred, but the court record does not disclose candidate-ranking methodology or the later witness's independence from the chosen lookalike. The unresolved evidentiary assurance question is specific to using this machine-derived lead for a potentially binding warrant, not merely to an inaccurate match.

clauses.source_paraphrase: A separately prepared photo lineup included Woodruff, and the victim selected her while stating that the choice was based on seeing the suspect in person for multiple hours.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Downstream human evidence can supply independent assurance only to the extent that its method and evidentiary basis can genuinely falsify rather than merely reinforce the machine-generated nomination.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The separately prepared lineup and victim identification are material evidence independent of the machine score itself, limiting any claim that the biometric inference alone acquired coercive authority; the occurrence remains informative to the class boundary because the machine nomination determined whose identity entered the downstream verification pathway.

The victim's separate photo-lineup identification followed the earlier 73-candidate facial search and peer-reviewed lead. A lineup was actually performed, so its later error cannot be recoded as an omitted verification step. The judicial record leaves the independence/possible contamination of that witness choice undecided; a particular mandatory omitted check or successfully verified non-tainted result is not proven.

clauses.source_paraphrase: On 4 February, Oliver sought arrest warrants after the witness identification and criminal-history review. A police captain and prosecutor approved the request; a magistrate signed the warrant.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A nomination, witness identification and authorised warrant are distinct evidentiary and decision stages. Judicial approval does not establish biometric correctness.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The arrest-warrant decision followed a model-initiated identity lead, human peer review, a subsequent witness photo lineup, and approvals by a police captain, prosecutor and magistrate. This is the actual binding-authority transition, but the court declined to decide whether the witness lineup was contaminated by the earlier facial-recognition result; independent authority sufficiency cannot be declared failure or success from the later mistaken identity alone.

At the actual warrant stage, a biometric lead and subsequent witness identification supported an arrest request reviewed by police command, a prosecutor and a magistrate. Those real checks matter, but their independent epistemic adequacy and the influence of the initial machine selection on the witness remain unsettled; the court expressly did not decide the taint theory. Reliance calibration at the consequential decision point is materially engaged without enough evidence to assert failure or success.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Woodruff was arrested on 16 February 2023 while eight months pregnant. After booking, Oliver recognised that the pregnancy and a tattoo contradicted the suspect identification. Woodruff remained in custody under the warrant.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Material contradictory identity evidence must remain capable of reopening and defeating an inferential identification before the inference produces a coercive effect.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: The advanced-pregnancy contradiction is material to whether the overall identity pathway remained adequately defeasible, but it does not by itself establish that a probabilistic machine inference was promoted into independent authority for arrest.

clauses.source_paraphrase: Oliver tried to obtain dismissal and told the arraignment magistrate they had the wrong person. Woodruff was released at about 19:00 on personal bond and received hospital treatment for contractions.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Recognition of a contradiction and a request to correct it are separate from effective release. The record of communication must not be replaced by an inference that no correction was attempted.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The officer reported mistaken identity to the prosecutor the next morning. The phone was returned on 17 February. A different prosecutor lacked dismissal information at the 27 February conference; the charges were dismissed on 7 March.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: Delivery, transfer between decision-makers and final disposition require separate evidence. One later recipient’s lack of information does not prove that an earlier communication was never made.

clauses.source_paraphrase: The City was dismissed by stipulation in November 2024. On 5 August 2025, the federal court granted the remaining officer summary judgment. It declined to decide the broader facial-recognition taint theory because Woodruff did not adopt that argument.
clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A judgment is bounded by the claims and arguments it decides. It does not settle an expressly undecided biometric-evidence theory.

notes: Preserve current Boundaries; an erroneous identification or later dismissal does not by itself establish automatic algorithmic authority. Legal outcome and taxonomy criteria remain distinct. No guilt or innocence determination is made.

previous_mapping.classification_basis: Investigators submitted a low-resolution surveillance image to facial recognition, obtained 73 candidates and selected Woodruff as an investigative lead through human narrowing and peer review. A witness then selected her from a separately prepared photo lineup; a captain, prosecutor and magistrate approved the subsequent warrant. The actual arrest was of the wrong person, but these intervening decisions prevent treating the model result as automatic arrest authority. The August 2025 court expressly did not decide whether the facial-recognition lead tainted the witness's later selection; the independent evidentiary validity of that authority basis is therefore unresolved. This materially engages Inferential Evidence–Authority Separation without demonstrating either impermissible promotion of model inference into binding authority or adequate independence of the later coercive decision.

previous_mapping.classification_basis: The facial-recognition search returned 73 candidates from a low-definition camera image, investigators narrowed that output to one suspect through peer review, and the witness then selected the same person in a separate lineup. The resulting information reached a high-consequence warrant workflow. The court record does not reconstruct the ranking methodology or establish whether the witness lineup was independent of the machine-generated lead; it also notes the later arrest was of the wrong person. These gaps materially engage the sufficiency of epistemic assurance for consequential reliance, but the warrant was not based on a facial match alone: intervening corroborative processes and judicial approvals were documented. The court found probable cause was not disproven on the submitted claims and left the lineup-taint question undecided. The exact unacceptable-assurance threshold or an affirmatively adequate independent reliance decision is not proven, so no failure or successful-invariant polarity is asserted.
